parameters.name: mnc

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: The sender ID which can be alphanumeric or numeric.

parameters.name: bulkId
parameters.description: Unique ID assigned to the request if messaging multiple recipients or sending multiple messages via a single API request. May contain multiple comma-separated values. Maximum length 2048 characters.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Unique message ID for which a log is requested. May contain multiple comma-separated values. Maximum length 2048 characters.

parameters.name: sentSince
parameters.description: The logs will only include messages sent after this date. Use it alongside sentUntil to specify a time range for the logs, but only up to the maximum limit of 1000 logs per call. Has the following format: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

parameters.name: sentUntil
parameters.description: The logs will only include messages sent before this date. Use it alongside sentSince to specify a time range for the logs, but only up to the maximum limit of 1000 logs per call. Has the following format: yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to include in logs. If not set, the latest 50 records are returned. Maximum limit value is 1000 and you can only access logs for the last 48h.

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description: Entity id used to send the message. For more details, see our [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application id used to send the message. For more details, see our [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

parameters.name: campaignReferenceId
parameters.description: ID of a campaign that was sent in the message. May contain multiple comma-separated values.

parameters.name: useCursor
parameters.description: Flag used to enable cursor-based pagination. When set to true, the system will use the cursor to fetch the next set of logs.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value which represents the current position in the data set. For the first request, this field shouldn't be defined. In subsequent requests, use the `nextCursor` value returned from the previous response to continue fetching data.

singleShift.description: Uses a single shift table which enhances only the extension table of the GSM default alphabet. Allows you to selectively improve character support without altering the entire message.

lockingShift.description: Uses a locking shift table which allows you to represent characters beyond the standard GSM default alphabet. This flexibility enables better language support.

dataCoding.description: Binary content data coding. The default value is (`0`) for GSM7. Example: (`8`) for  Unicode data.

hex.description: Hexadecimal string. This is the representation of your binary data. Two hex digits represent one byte. They should be separated by the space character.

gotchas: Send the API key as 'Authorization: App <API_KEY>' — the prefix App; Bearer is only for OAuth 2.0 access tokens. Infobip API keys have a predefined expiry date and can be revoked at any time; a missing or invalid credential answers 401.
The OpenAPI lists these API key scopes for this endpoint (x-scopes): sms:manage, sms:logs:read. Give the key a matching scope when you create it.

Each Infobip account has its own base URL, xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown once you log in to the Infobip API Resource hub. Set it in INFOBIP_BASE_URL (https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com in this spec is a placeholder). It identifies your account, the API key authenticates it.
Logs cover the last 48 hours only, at most 1000 per call (limit defaults to 50). For more, enable useCursor and pass nextCursor back as cursor.
To check whether a message was delivered, use delivery reports (webhook or get_sms_delivery_reports), not logs.
bulkId, messageId and campaignReferenceId accept several values (2048 characters at most).

List query parameters are declared style form, explode true in the OpenAPI (repeated keys: status=A&status=B, as this example sends them) while their descriptions say comma-separated values. With a single value both readings match.

The OpenAPI documents no error body for this endpoint (401, 403, 429, 500 have no schema): handle errors on the HTTP status. The 401 body shown on the authentication page is { requestError: { serviceException: { messageId, text } } }.
A 429 means the endpoint's rate limit was hit; limits differ per endpoint. Retry with exponential backoff and honour the Retry-After header when present.
